$comment: Copy to config/cambridge.json and fill in. The real file is git-ignored
because it holds camera access-authentication credentials.
Read username/password off each body at:

camd.$comment: The C++ daemon. Loopback only by design — nothing outside this Mac talks to it directly.
camd.$comment_ws: WebSocket shares the REST port via HTTP upgrade; one port, one listener.

connection.$comment: Phase 2 lifecycle tuning. A dead camera must never affect the other two.
connection.$comment_backoff: Caps at 15s so a camera that comes back mid-take rejoins fast. The brief's target is reconnect within ~10s of link restore.

cambridge.$comment: The Node app server and web UI. Binds all interfaces so the iPad on the production VLAN can reach it.

logging.$comment: Every state change, timestamped, to a rotating file. This is what we read the morning after something went wrong on a shoot.

atem.$comment: Tally from a Blackmagic ATEM. Read-only — CamBridge never sends the switcher a command. Leave enabled false if there is no switcher.
atem.$comment_mapping: Which ATEM input each camera is plugged into, as numbered on the switcher. Used by both tally and Link.
atem.$comment_link: ATEM Link: let a Blackmagic hardware panel or the Camera page drive Sony exposure. Still switcher-to-camera only — CamBridge never sends the switcher anything. OFF by default because the decoder's packet layout has not yet been confirmed against real hardware.
atem.$comment_logRaw: Capture mode. Logs every camera-control block the switcher sends, as hex next to how CamBridge read it, without acting on any of it. Turn this on first, move one control at a time on the panel, and check the two agree before setting link true.
atem.$comment_coalesceMs: A panel wheel emits dozens of positions a second; only the newest is worth sending. Raise if a camera still struggles to keep up.

visca.$comment: Accept VISCA so a hardware joystick or controller panel can drive the cameras. Off by default: no reason to have a socket open for hardware that is not there.
visca.$comment_mapping: VISCA address for each camera. Omit the whole mapping to fall back to camera order, which is right for a single-camera setup.

alarms.$comment: When to warn about a card filling or a battery running down. Chosen against how long it takes to act, not round numbers: five minutes of card is about the time to notice, swap it and get back.

auth.$comment: Who can control the cameras. With both PINs null the panel is OPEN — anyone on this network has full control and can read the camera passwords. Set a PIN from the Setup tab rather than editing this by hand; PINs are stored salted and hashed and never in the clear.
auth.$comment_roles: Operators can drive every camera. Admin is needed for what outlasts a shoot: adopting, forgetting or re-credentialing a camera, and quitting the app. With no adminPin set, one PIN means one level of access.
auth.$comment_tokens: Machine clients — Bitfocus Companion, scripts — send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' instead of a PIN, because they cannot answer a prompt. Map each token to the role it carries. Treat these like passwords.

cameras.label: FX3 — Wide
cameras.$comment_fingerprint: Access Authen. Info also shows a fingerprint. Whether the SDK needs it is a Phase 1 open question; record it here once we know.
